lessons.title: Gradual change with につれて
lessons.summary: Practiced describing two changes that progress together, made original sentences, translated reading and listening ideas, and finished with a personal Japanese paragraph.

grammar.explanation: As one change progresses, another related change also develops. The result clause normally describes a change rather than a deliberate action.
grammar.example: 経験を積むにつれて、仕事の進め方が分かってきた。

sources.label: The Japan Foundation: につれて／につれ
Meguro Language Center: JLPT N2 grammar

activities.title: Opening sentence · expressing a change over time

items.original: 日本語を話すのが緊張でしたが、今は同僚と話せるようになる。
items.correction: 日本語を話すときは緊張していましたが、今は同僚と話せるようになりました。
items.alternative: 最初は日本語を話すのが不安でしたが、今では同僚とも話せるようになりました。
items.note: 緊張 is commonly used with する: 緊張する／緊張している. For an achieved change in the past, use 話せるようになりました.
All three choices fit the topic. 徐々に is an adverb; 増加 is a noun and is also used as 増加する.

activities.title: Build sentences with につれて

items.original: 経験を積むにつれて、仕事の進め方が分かってきた。
items.correction: 経験を積むにつれて、仕事の進め方が分かってきた。
items.alternative: 経験を重ねるにつれて、仕事の進め方が少しずつ分かってきた。
items.note: Natural and grammatically sound. 分かってきた emphasizes that understanding developed over time.

items.original: 日本語を勉強するにつれて、漢字も読めるようになる。
items.correction: 日本語を勉強するにつれて、漢字も読めるようになってきた。
items.alternative: 日本語を勉強するにつれて、読める漢字が少しずつ増えてきた。
items.note: The original is correct as a general tendency or prediction. 〜ようになってきた fits a change already underway.

items.original: Even though he could memorised the words. Over time, being unable to use the memorised words, he did not become better in conversation.
items.correction: Although he memorized the words, he couldn't use them in conversation, so he didn't get any better at speaking.
items.note: After could, use the base verb (could memorize). Here, although connects the contrast, and get better at speaking is more natural than become better in conversation.

items.original: He could inferred the meaning of articles even though they may contain words that he did not know
items.correction: He could infer the meaning of an article even if it contained words he didn't know.
items.note: After could, use infer, not inferred. The past-tense clause keeps the sentence consistent.

items.original: につれて　少しずつ    he feels less anxious about speaking Japanese
items.correction: 日本語を話す練習を続けるにつれて、話すことへの不安が少しずつ減ってきた。
items.alternative: As he kept practicing speaking Japanese, he gradually felt less anxious about it.
items.note: 少しずつ works naturally with a gradual change. 不安が減る describes anxiety decreasing.

items.original: He could catch the flow of of the news even though he could not understand every word
items.correction: He could follow the general flow of the news even though he couldn't understand every word.
items.note: Use follow the flow of the news or follow the general idea. The repeated of was removed.

items.original: He tried to look up every word that he did not understand, he could not finish the podcast before reaching his stop
items.correction: He tried to look up every unfamiliar word, so he couldn't finish the podcast before he reached his stop.
items.note: The original joined two complete clauses with a comma. Adding so makes the cause-and-result relationship clear.

items.original: He would try to infer the meaning of the content from context, and only look up the meaning of words that he is curious, instead of every word
items.correction: He tried to infer the meaning from context and looked up only the words he was curious about, instead of looking up every word.
items.note: Say curious about a word. Keeping the two past-tense actions parallel makes the sentence smoother.

items.original: cafetalkで日本人の先生と話すにつれて、聴く力が徐々に強くなりました。ドラマを見ると、分からない内容を推測できるようになりました。もっと頑張ろうと思います。
items.correction: Cafetalkで日本人の先生と話すにつれて、聞き取りの力が徐々に伸びてきました。ドラマを見ると、分からない内容も推測できるようになりました。もっと頑張ろうと思います。
items.alternative: Cafetalkで日本人の先生と話す機会を重ねるうちに、聞き取りが少しずつ上達してきました。ドラマを見ていると、分からない部分も文脈から推測できるようになりました。これからも頑張りたいです。
items.note: 聞く力が強くなる is understandable, but 聞き取りの力が伸びる or 聞き取りが上達する is a more natural collocation. につれて suits paired gradual changes; うちに can emphasize a change that developed through repeated experience.
